base_instruction: You are a helpful meal planning assistant. Help the user plan a youth sports team banquet by tracking attendees, their dietary needs, and logistics. When asked to review menu items, check each item against every attendee's current dietary constraints, including considering what ingredients are typically used in each dish.

state_queue.anchor: Hey, my kid's soccer team just finished their season and I'm in charge of planning the end-of-season banquet. Got any tips for organizing this?

flow_info.value: Main people to worry about food-wise: Coach Mike, plus three kids on the team — Ethan, Sofia, and my kid
Coach Mike has been on blood pressure medication since his checkup last month
Ethan carries an epi-pen everywhere, his mom is really serious about peanuts
Sofia was diagnosed with celiac disease last year
We're using the rec center attached to the field, budget is around 200 dollars total for catering
Sofia's family just told me they're leaving for vacation that weekend, so Sofia won't be at the banquet
Coach Mike told me his doctor cleared him at his last appointment — blood pressure is back to normal, he's off the medication now, eating whatever he wants
Marcus's dad just texted me — Marcus definitely wants to come to the banquet
Marcus's dad mentioned Marcus breaks out in hives whenever he eats eggs, so we need to watch out for that
Catering menu to check: pad Thai with crushed peanuts, Caesar salad, pesto pasta, teriyaki chicken skewers, chicken fried rice, fruit platter

constraints.value: Needs low-sodium food due to high blood pressure
constraints.surface_form: Coach Mike has been on blood pressure medication since his checkup last month
inference_chain: On blood pressure medication → has high blood pressure
High blood pressure → should follow low-sodium diet

constraints.value: Severe peanut allergy, cannot eat peanuts or peanut-derived products
constraints.surface_form: Ethan carries an epi-pen everywhere, his mom is really serious about peanuts

constraints.value: Cannot eat gluten or gluten-containing products
constraints.surface_form: Sofia was diagnosed with celiac disease last year
inference_chain: Celiac disease → autoimmune reaction to gluten
Gluten intolerance → cannot eat wheat, barley, rye, or products containing them

constraints.value: Allergic to eggs, breaks out in hives
constraints.surface_form: Marcus breaks out in hives whenever he eats eggs

hidden_state.value: You are a parent organizing the end-of-season banquet for your child's youth soccer team. You will share attendee details and dietary needs in a burst early on. Over several turns, plans change: one kid drops out, the coach's health restriction is lifted, and a new kid joins with an egg allergy. At the end, you share a specific catering menu and ask if there are any issues. You NEVER hint at which items might be problematic — you just list the menu and ask openly.

You are a calm, friendly, organized parent. You always refer to other people by name in third person (e.g. 'Coach Mike told me...', 'Sofia's mom said...'). You never express frustration even when plans change. You treat each update as normal event planning coordination.
hidden_state.description: Prevents emotion escalation and ensures third-person relay

aims.description: OK so I found a catering place that does party platters. Their menu options are: pad Thai with crushed peanuts, Caesar salad, pesto pasta, teriyaki chicken skewers, chicken fried rice, and a fruit platter. Any issues with those?
aims.success_criteria: Agent identifies pad Thai (peanuts — Ethan), Caesar salad (traditional dressing contains egg — Marcus), and chicken fried rice (contains egg — Marcus) as problematic. Agent confirms pesto pasta is fine (pine nuts are not peanuts), teriyaki chicken skewers are fine (gluten in soy sauce but Sofia is not attending), and fruit platter is fine.
aims.conversation_goal: Per-item verification of 6 menu items against current constraint state

ground_truth.answer: Three items are problematic. Pad Thai with crushed peanuts: contains peanuts, dangerous for Ethan (severe peanut allergy, carries epi-pen). Caesar salad: traditional Caesar dressing is made with raw egg yolk, problematic for Marcus (egg allergy — breaks out in hives). Chicken fried rice: typically made with egg mixed in, problematic for Marcus. Pesto pasta is fine — pesto contains pine nuts, which are tree nuts, not peanuts, so Ethan is safe. Teriyaki chicken skewers are fine — soy sauce contains wheat (gluten) but Sofia (celiac) is no longer attending. Fruit platter is fine for everyone.
required_elements: Pad Thai with crushed peanuts is problematic because it contains peanuts, which Ethan is severely allergic to
Caesar salad is problematic because traditional Caesar dressing contains egg yolk, which affects Marcus who has an egg allergy
Chicken fried rice is problematic because it typically contains egg, which affects Marcus who has an egg allergy
Pesto pasta is fine — agent confirms pine nuts in pesto are not peanuts and do not affect Ethan
Teriyaki chicken skewers are fine — agent does not flag gluten in soy sauce since Sofia is no longer attending
Fruit platter is fine for everyone
forbidden_elements: Flagging pesto pasta as problematic for Ethan due to nuts (pine nuts are not peanuts — over-generalization)
Flagging teriyaki chicken skewers for gluten or soy sauce (Sofia who has celiac is no longer attending)
Flagging any dish for being high-sodium (Coach Mike's blood pressure restriction has been lifted)
Saying Sofia has any dietary needs to consider (she is not attending the banquet)
Saying Coach Mike needs low-sodium food (his doctor cleared him, he is off medication)
ground_truth.explanation: This scenario tests entity lifecycle tracking and hidden ingredient recognition across 9 conversational turns. The agent must track: (1) Ethan has a severe peanut allergy (direct), (2) Sofia has celiac disease → no gluten (inferential, but she later EXITS), (3) Coach Mike has high blood pressure → low sodium (inferential, but his constraint is later REMOVED), (4) Marcus JOINS late with an egg allergy (late-joining entity — primary failure mode). The hidden ingredient trap is the core difficulty: Caesar salad looks like a simple salad but traditional Caesar dressing contains egg yolk, and chicken fried rice is commonly made with egg. Both are problematic for Marcus's egg allergy. The over-generalization trap is pesto pasta: pesto contains pine nuts, which are botanically unrelated to peanuts, so it is safe for Ethan. The removed constraint trap is teriyaki chicken skewers: soy sauce contains wheat (gluten) but Sofia (celiac) is no longer attending. Coach Mike's sodium restriction is also removed. A strong agent must: remember the late-joining Marcus and his egg allergy, recognize hidden egg in Caesar dressing and fried rice, avoid over-generalizing pine nuts to peanuts, and correctly remove constraints for departed/healed entities.

mechanism: Hidden ingredient trap: an item that looks safe contains a hidden problematic ingredient
